**Structure:** Manifesto-into-framework video: opens with a personal motto, myth-busts the "glamorous digital nomad" narrative, argues for generalism over specialization, then formally introduces the "one person business" model, its four pillars (branding, content, offer, marketing) and three entry paths (skill-based, development-based, both), closing with a product pitch and subscribe CTA.

**Structure:** Long-form theory lecture: redefines intelligence via cybernetics (goal-seeking feedback loops) rather than IQ, argues goals shape identity and perception, then walks through the nine stages of ego/psychological development (pre-conventional through conventional -- conformist, expert, achiever -- to post-conventional -- pluralist, strategist, construct-aware -- to the transcendent unitive stage), mapping public figures (Jordan Peterson, Alan Watts, Hamza) onto the model, closing with book/course plugs.
**Framing:** Academic-lecture framing that borrows heavily from named frameworks and thinkers (cybernetics, Csikszentmihalyi's flow, Maxwell Maltz's Psycho-Cybernetics, Ken Wilber, Susanne Cook-Greuter's ego development theory, Spiral Dynamics) to position the video as a rigorous synthesis rather than opinion, while explicitly self-aware about using clickbait titles as a funnel into deeper material.

**Structure:** Definitional-critique-into-framework video: opens with a personal origin story about early fitness YouTubers, critiques and redefines influencer/creator/personal-brand as hollowed-out categories, proposes "be paid to be yourself" as the alternative (using Jordan Peterson as the model), then delivers a four-part system (positive aim, audience, project-to-product, iteration) and a four-pillar creative-work framework (brand, content, product, promotion) including his "core notes" content-ideation method, closing with course/software plugs.
**Framing:** Elder-statesman-of-the-creator-economy framing: positions Dan as present since the "golden age" of creator content, diagnosing its decline before prescribing the fix, and repeatedly reframes shallow-seeming tactics (engagement groups, niches, social media itself) as deep when done with the right philosophy.

**Structure:** Extended-metaphor video: opens on the flow state as the "optimal human experience," argues life is a game already being played by society's rules (the "macro game"), then breaks down how to consciously design one's own game -- set a hierarchy of goals, create a frame (rules and mechanics), and balance the anxiety/boredom skill-challenge curve (citing Csikszentmihalyi's Flow) -- illustrated throughout with World of Warcraft mechanics, closing with course/community plugs.
**Framing:** Nostalgic-gamer-to-life-philosophy framing: uses Dan's own teenage World of Warcraft character-creation memory as the throughline, translating a familiar gaming vocabulary (leveling up, NPCs, guilds, professions) into a self-development system to make abstract flow-state psychology feel intuitive to a gaming-literate audience.

**Structure:** Framework-catalog video: opens by naming persuasive communication as the base skill under every other marketable skill, then walks through his "Ten Commandments of engagement" for capturing attention (specific numbers, pattern interrupts, negativity bias, group call-outs, problem/benefit call-outs, social proof, confidence, active voice, warnings) with worked tweet examples for most, then covers what holds attention (story structure, formatting, novel perspectives) and what creates engagement (education, inspiration, entertainment), closing with a book preorder and course plug.
**Framing:** Toolbox-of-tactics framing: an unusually list-heavy, example-driven video (each commandment paired with a real high-performing tweet Dan wrote) that treats persuasion as a set of learnable, swappable mechanisms rather than an innate talent, including a moment of self-critique where he revises one of his own viral tweets on camera.

**Structure:** Long-form flow-state treatise structured as a multi-part essay: opens defining flow via Csikszentmihalyi, uses his own World of Warcraft character-creation memory as an extended metaphor for identity/culture/leveling, covers psychic entropy and the mind-as-computer/RAM metaphor, cites Steven Kotler's five intrinsic drivers, then delivers a five-step practical system (create a clarity catalyst/project, learn as you build, teach what you learn, expand into a new level of mind, make cross-domain connections), closing with book/newsletter/podcast plugs.
**Framing:** Cumulative-synthesis framing: explicitly the most theory-dense and citation-heavy video in the set (Csikszentmihalyi, Alan Watts, David Hawkins, Ken Wilber, Steven Kotler, Robert Greene), presented as connecting all of Dan's prior video concepts into one unified thesis, with an aside noting the video itself was an 8-12 week project used as a live example of the flow system it teaches.

**Structure:** Long-form podcast interview (not a solo monologue): opens with a short host introduction framing Devon Eriksen's background and the conversation's themes, then proceeds as a two-person dialogue covering education/agency (the seven liberal arts, self-limiting identity beliefs), AI as "artificial stupidity" versus human executive function, property/ownership and selling time versus scaling, and self-publishing versus traditional publishers (the Kickstarter-funded audiobook story), closing with a direct call-to-action to aspiring authors and plugs for Eriksen's book/Substack.
**Framing:** Guest-authority interview framing distinct from Dan's solo essay-style videos: Dan mostly asks questions and connects Eriksen's points back to his own recurring concepts (ego development stages, the niche/audience-as-trust argument), while Eriksen supplies most of the original theory (agency, self-limiting beliefs, artificial stupidity) and personal narrative (leaving software engineering, rejecting a traditional publishing deal).

**Structure:** Origin-story-into-tactics video: opens with Dan's own failed digital-art Instagram phase (2,500 followers, then burnout) as a credibility-building anecdote, lays out a four-step growth framework (write persuasive content, get eyes on it, iterate with data, build long-form depth), then details four "traffic mechanisms" (replies, quote posts, reposts, manual DMs) and three growth-control strategies (short-to-long-form funneling, curation/remixing bigger creators, paid growth/masterminds), closing with a defensive rebuttal to critics of paid-growth tactics and a book plug.
**Framing:** Blunt-insider-confession framing: unusually profanity-heavy and defensive in tone, explicitly pre-empting and rebutting the "engagement groups/paid growth are inauthentic" objection at length, positioning candor about unglamorous tactics (paying for reposts, mastermind groups) as more honest than pretending organic growth alone works.

**Structure:** Foundational one-person-business video (one of Dan's earliest in this set): opens with a Naval Ravikant quote and a case against chasing billion-dollar-startup dreams, explains the two entry routes (skill-based vs. development-based), defines the three components of a one-person business (brand, content, monetization), then delivers his five-step "entrepreneurial method" (find a problem, learn to solve it, document it, systemize the process, share your discoveries), closing with a reflective aside on raising personal and collective consciousness and course/planner plugs.
**Framing:** Early-channel confessional framing: leans on Dan's own disclosed sales history ("$100,000 plus of almost everything") and a self-aware acknowledgment of the follower-count "gap" perception to argue anyone can replicate the method, closing on a more philosophical register (consciousness-raising, a Kabbalah quote) than his later, more tactically dense videos.
